verdict.rationale: Clerk's changelog describes a standards-based grant that lets CLIs and other devices that cannot open a browser ask a user to approve access from a browser-capable device, without entering credentials on the original device. That is the OAuth device authorization flow the story describes, delivered by Clerk's own OAuth implementation, so the core of the story is met. Missing for 10: in-depth first-party docs (setup, polling and token lifetimes), explicit naming of the device authorization grant and headless-agent usage, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can authenticate CLIs and headless agents via the OAuth device authorization flow instead of pasting long-lived secrets

citations.quote: The grant provides a standards-based flow for applications that cannot open a browser or easily accept text input. CLIs, TVs, game consoles, and other devices can ask a user to approve access from a browser-capable device without entering their credentials on the original device.
